articles.title: Google TV Streamer review: smarter than your average set-top box
articles.summary: Google’s latest iteration on the Chromecast is the Google TV Streamer 4K — a $100 set-top streaming box that doubles as a smart home hub.
articles.body: It took Google a few years, a couple of pivots, and multiple name changes, but the company has finally built an excellent operating system for watching TV. The Google TV interface — running on top of the Android TV OS (Google’s branding chaos remains undefeated) — has already been doing a really nice job of making it easy to find what you’re looking for and constantly recommending new stuff to watch. But the Chromecast streaming dongle it ran on hasn’t been able to keep up. Now, Google TV is getting the hardware to match. The Google TV Streamer 4K, which goes on sale tomorrow for $99.99, is an upgrade in every way over the Chromecast with Google TV. There’s a new processor, a built-in ethernet port, plus double the RAM and four times the storage of the Chromecast. It supports Matter for your smart home, and a Thread radio makes it a Thread border router, which Jen will tell you more about in a bit. All of this means Google finally has an up-to-date set-top box that shares streaming and smart home duties. Google hasn’t provided details of the new processor (there are reports it’s the same MediaTek chip the Fire TV Stick 4K uses), but it’s clearly not as overpowered as the more expensive Apple TV with the literal chip of an iPhone inside. Still, it’s good to see Google getting serious in this space. [Product: Google TV Streamer (4K) | With this new hardware, the dongle is gone. This is a grown-up set-top box, designed to sit out on your media console. As slabs of plastic go, it’s fine; my only real note here is that you should buy the dark “hazel” color. I opted for the lighter “porcelain” for my review unit, and it’s quite noticeable sitting underneath my TV. I don’t mind that Google switched from dongle to box — I’m happy to have made that trade for the Streamer’s ethernet port and smart home controls, plus the really handy button that pings your remote when it’s lost in the couch — but there’s a reason virtually all TV gadgets are black. And if you’re coming from a Chromecast and looking to keep that visual simplicity, it’ll be easy to tape or Velcro the Streamer to the back of your TV. While slightly larger, the remote is virtually identical to the one that shipped with the Chromecast with Google TV four years ago. It does HDMI-CEC and IR controls, has voice control, runs on AAA batteries, and now has a mappable shortcut button. I’m a little less enthusiastic about the remote than my colleague Chris Welch was back in 2020: I wish the D-pad and the select button were a little better differentiated, and the power button is too far away from everything else. But by and large, it’s a fine remote, and its smooth, round edges feel good to fiddle with. [Image: The Streamer is designed to sit out on your TV console, which should help its smart home radios get better exposure. Getting the Streamer ready to watch shows and movies is simple enough and roughly the same process as any other set-top box. You do most of the setup in the Google Home app on your phone, which is how you log it in to your Google account and connect the Streamer to your smart home devices. (You can also do things directly on the screen by clicking around with the remote, but it’ll take forever. Your phone is your friend.) One particularly nice feature: as part of the setup process, the Home app asks which streaming services you use and then automatically downloads them to the box. --- Google TV Streamer specs * Price: $99.99 * Colors: white and gray * Resolution: up to 4K HDR, 60fps * Video Formats: Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10 Plus, HLG * Audio Formats: Dolby Digital, Dolby Digital Plus, Dolby Atmos * Connectivity: Wi-Fi (2.4GHz / 5GHz), Bluetooth 5.2, Matter, Thread border router * Memory: 4GB * Storage: 32GB * Ports: USB-C, HDMI 2.1, ethernet * Google Voice Remote uses two AAA batteries and Bluetooth IR --- The Streamer can handle 4K video with Dolby Vision and does Dolby Atmos audio as well. If your TV and audio gear support it, you can also set up the Streamer’s remote to control your other devices. You’re also prompted during setup to create multiple profiles, including kid-specific ones — hooray! — and to pick whether you want your screensaver to be from your Google Photos or some AI-generated art. (Jen asked it to generate images of a South Carolina sunset, and the AI made sunset “photos” that looked like they were taken on the worst camera you could find.) The whole setup process, including a necessary software update, took me maybe 10 minutes. The fastest way I’ve found to do almost anything on the Streamer is via voice. In more nonsensical branding, the Streamer’s voice assistant is Google Assistant and not Gemini, even though Google says it’s Gemini technology under the hood. What matters is that Google TV handles voice commands mostly very well. “Play Industry on Max” took me exactly where it should. “Show me Mission: Impossible movies” brought them all up, in order. “Play Brooklyn Nine-Nine” triggered a menu with all the places I can watch the show. It’s not perfect: “Play ‘Hot Ones’ on YouTube” didn’t work, but “find ‘Hot Ones’ videos on YouTube” did, and while it’s handy to have Google Assistant tell me all the places Brooklyn Nine-Nine is available, it should be able to learn that I’m watching the show on Peacock and just take me there. In general, though, if you know what you want to watch — and especially if you know what service it’s on — there’s no faster way to navigate any set-top box than via Google Assistant here. And, of course, the Streamer is still a Chromecast, so you can use your phone to find and cast stuff to your screen as well. [Image: The redesigned remote is larger than the Chromecast with Google TV counterpart and features a new mappable button (bottom right) that can either call up the smart home panel, switch inputs, or be used to summon a favorite app. Flipping around the homescreen looking for something to watch, I encountered the most disappointing thing about the Streamer: it’s not fast. It’s not slow, and it’s noticeably faster than the lag-plagued Chromecast from a few years ago, but it’s definitely not fast. The five-year-old Nvidia Shield is noticeably zippier and smoother as I open and close apps and scroll the interface, as is the latest Apple TV. Given how much Google hyped the processor and RAM upgrades on this device and how much more expensive it is as a result, it’s a little disappointing. It also makes me nervous for the future given the Chromecast with Google TV’s reputation for degrading performance over time. But today, it’s fast enough. And it’s when you don’t know what you want to watch that Google TV really shines — on the Streamer and elsewhere. It aggregates FAST channels from its own Freeplay service and more, so there’s lots of live and free stuff to watch. The “Trending on Google” row is extremely zeitgeist-y and fun. Just given what it already knows about you, from YouTube and Search and elsewhere, plus the ongoing work it’s doing with Gemini, Google has a nearly insurmountable advantage when it comes to recommending stuff you’ll like, and it shows. That’s what makes the Google TV Streamer an excellent streaming device. But what takes it over the top is its smart home features — and for that, my colleague Jen has the details below. Smart TV, smart home [Image: The new smart home panel appears on the right of the TV screen. It allows you to control smart home devices like lights and view livestreams from connected cameras using the remote. Streaming may be in the name, but the Google TV Streamer also quietly doubles as a very capable smart home hub. I’m a big proponent of marrying the smart TV with the smart home; it’s just a natural fit. With Matter controller and Thread border router chops, the Streamer can connect smart home devices like lights, locks, and thermostats to Google Home, just like Google’s Nest Hubs can. But thanks to a built-in ethernet port and a new smart home panel, it’s a more robust option for putting at the heart of your smart home than the Nest Hub (second-gen) or Nest Hub Max. It’s also much snappier than either of those. In fact, the Google TV Streamer is the only Google Home hub that supports Matter, Thread, ethernet, Google Assistant voice control (through the remote), and smart display functions (through your TV) all in one package, making it my new recommendation for the best smart home hub for Google Home. [Image: The Streamer has a soft cloth base for sitting on your TV console and features three ports: HDMI (with support for 2.1), ethernet (up to a gigabit), and USB-C for power. The small button to the right resets the device with a long press and activates the speaker in the remote with a short press. With the new smart home panel, the Streamer brings direct control of the smart home to Google TV for the first time outside of voice. The panel, which first appeared on Google’s Pixel Tablet (which should have been a smart home hub but isn’t), pops up on your TV screen to offer shortcuts to turn off lights or view your cameras with the press of a button. The Home panel takes a lot of design cues from the Apple TV, which — let’s face it — the entire device does. But I was pleased to see that it offers more flexibility, more options, and is more intuitive than the Apple TV’s version for smart home control. --- Streamer side notes * The Google TV Streamer comes with a USB-C power cable and power brick but no ethernet cable or HDMI 2.1 cable, so if you don’t have any spare cables, factor the purchase of those into the price. * It only supports Wi-Fi 5. This is maybe not an issue for most people, but for smart homes with lots of devices on the network, the more efficient Wi-Fi 6 or the option to run your TV on the 6GHz band with Wi-Fi 6E could be beneficial. Ethernet does help here, though. * You can’t use Nest speakers for TV audio from the Streamer, though you can pair Bluetooth devices like earbuds to it and add the TV speakers to audio groups in the Home app. * The remote’s Find My feature also works with voice control. Ask a Nest speaker, “Where’s the TV remote?” and it will beep away. * The Thread radio can be enabled and disabled in Settings — useful for troubleshooting any Thread network issues. * The Streamer can show Gemini-powered Personalized Results on the ambient screen, but that apparently takes some time to appear, as none showed up in our testing. * Long-pressing the Home button on the remote opens the Streamer Settings, a great quality-of-life feature for reviewers constantly tinkering with settings! * The new voice remote also works with the Chromecast with Google TV. --- The panel is based around the Google Home app interface, so it feels familiar. It has the same fixed shortcuts that take you to cameras, lights, and climate controls. Then there’s the same scrollable list of your “Favorites,” which can include everything from individual devices or cameras to groups and automations. I was impressed at how fast the panel was for controlling lights and automations — the lights in my living room turned on and off instantly, and a Movie Time scene controlling multiple devices executed in seconds — much faster than using voice control through the Chromecast or a Nest speaker. In my few days of testing the device, I found myself picking up the remote to use the Streamer to control my lights more than using my phone. Thanks to the option to program the new shortcut button on the remote to open the panel, it got me to the controls faster. It’s also nice not to have to reach for the distraction that is my phone while watching TV. Pulling up live feeds from connected cameras took a bit longer, but I’m fine with that now that there is finally the option to have your video doorbell show automatically on the TV when someone’s at the door. This is a feature Fire TVs and Apple TVs have had for years. On the Streamer, a small picture-in-picture appears in the top right, showing a snapshot of your visitor, with the option to click “view” to see the full-screen feed. (You have to be quick here since it goes away in a few seconds.) The picture-in-picture part only works with Google Nest doorbells (I tested it with the battery-powered Nest Doorbell), but Google says you will still get a text notification on the TV when using any doorbell compatible with the Google Home app and can then pull up a livestream. [Image: The Google TV Streamer is an excellent blend of smart home and smart TV. The biggest downside of the Home panel is that you can’t customize it; it’s persistent across devices. What I select for the Favorites section in the Google Home app on my phone is what shows up on my TV. It would be nice to choose the cameras I want to see and the lights and automations I want to access based on which room the Streamer is in. But that’s a minor quibble. The addition of support for Matter and Thread, a mesh networking protocol designed for IoT devices, elevates the Streamer to true smart home hub status. Thread is one of two wireless protocols the new Matter smart home standard supports, and it creates a more reliable communication pathway for low-power smart devices like lights, locks, and sensors throughout your home. Current Google Nest Hubs and Google Nest Wifi routers are also Thread border routers, and the more border routers you have, the more reliable your network will be (as long as they’re all from the same company, for now). Additionally, Google’s new Home runtime feature, which is coming to its Google Home hubs later this year, will enable direct local control of gadgets over Matter. This should significantly reduce latency when issuing commands to smart devices. It’s these smart home capabilities that make the Streamer worth purchasing over the $50 Google TV with Chromecast or Walmart’s Onn 4K Pro. Neither of those works with Thread, and neither can automatically pull up a livestream on your TV when someone rings your doorbell or let you control smart lights and adjust your thermostat on the big screen. David and I agree: this is the best set-top box Google has made yet. It’s not some earth-shattering new idea or game-changing improvement on the formula, but Google TV is the best streaming UI on the market, and the hardware doesn’t hold the streamer back this time. Combined with an easy-to-use smart home panel and Matter and Thread support, all for under $100, this is the set-top box we’d recommend to most people. --- Agree to continue: Google TV Streamer 4K (2024) Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we started counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. To use the Google TV Streamer 4K, you must agree to: * Google Terms of Service * Google Play Terms of Service * Google Privacy Policy (included in ToS) * Google Device Arbitration Agreement (you can opt out by following the instructions in that agreement.) Streaming services also have their own terms of service and privacy policies. Final tally: at least three mandatory agreements. --- Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: Wardogs Season 2 Adds a New Gambling Mechanic That Lets You Bet on Yourself
articles.summary: Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system which will allow players to bet on their own performance.
articles.body:
Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system that will allow players to bet on their own performances.

The new season of Wardogs, due to launch on October 15, features a bunch of new content, most notably a new weather system that adds rain to matches . Another major mechanic lets players win big, or lose tons of cash. It's called the Wager Vendor, and it allows players to bet on themselves. If you think you can kill 20 people in a match, make a bet, and you will be rewarded. However, if you fail, you will lose cash. The harder your challenge is, the more you stand to win.

Speaking exclusively to IGN about the new system, developer Bulkhead noted that it technically won't be available to players as soon as the season launches, as they'll have to unlock it by building up cash.

"The Wager Vendor basically lets you bet on your own performance," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "So if I want to go in and say, 'I'm going to get 20 kills this match,' you then set that in your Wager Vendor, you then set the condition so I can say, 'Oh, I need to go and kill 20 people with my fists.' Okay, that's a bit harder, but that's when the odds go up. And then you set that as a condition and you can add multiple conditions."

"If you're a really good player and you're really smart about building your wager, you can make big money, but you can also lose big money," added senior producer Kane Allard.

Players can get pretty specific with these wagers. However, the more restrictions you put on yourself, the harder it will be to accomplish.

"Conditions-wise, it can even go down to as minute as, 'I need to get five kills, they're all head shots, all with the AK74M, and they all have to be in the hot zone, and my loadout has to cost less than 20K,'" said Allard. "You can build that wager and you can maybe earn double of what you put down, but that's a lot of restrictions that you're putting on yourself, and there's going to be players that may be also trying the same thing, and it just adds a little bit more tension to the game."

This not only spices up the gameplay, but it can also be extremely rewarding for players who are trying to build up some cash. If you're playing medic, you could theoretically give yourself a bonus for reviving 30 players. This then incentivizes medics to help their team more. It'll be intersting to see how this changes player behavior, but it sounds like it could be a lot of fun.

Call of Duty had a far less detailed version of this system in 2010's Call of Duty: Black Ops. Players could unlock items with an in-game currency and go into high stakes party games, such as Gun Game and One in the Chamber, to try and earn more money. GTA Online also has a betting system, allowing players to bet on players they think will perform best in PvP modes.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: New Avatar Show in Development as Seven Havens Renewed for Seasons 3 and 4
articles.summary: A brand-new show in the Avatar: The Last Airbender universe is in the works, focusing on an Avatar from the water tribe named Kuruk.
articles.body:
A brand-new show in the Avatar: The Last Airbender universe is in the works, focusing on an Avatar from the water tribe named Kuruk.

The show is titled Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos and takes place three generations before Avatar Aang. Avatar co-creators Bryan Konietzko and Michael Dante DiMartino are listed as showrunners, with Avatar Studios and Nickelodeon Animation Studios handling production.

As reported by Variety , the show’s logline is as follows: “A rebellious teenage Avatar bucks thousands of years of tradition by choosing to learn the four elements through globetrotting adventures, staying one step ahead of his angry teacher, rowdy pirates, and chaotic spirits – all while helping the world in his own unique ways.”

Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos First-Look Images

Paramount also shared a few first-look images at Avatar Kuruk at New York Comic Con, which show Kurk waterbending, taking in a view of the Northern Water Tribe Capital, and an image of his koala-like animal companion, Nikik.

Taking a shot at recent online leaks about the project during the NYCC panel, Konietzko said it will be the franchise’s first action-comedy. The panel also pulled back the curtain on the Avatar shows' production process, showing fans a special “script to screen” clip that was a visual explainer on how a scene of the series moves from the printed page to finished animation. The clip is now available on YouTube for all Avatar fans to enjoy.

Fighting game fans got their own moment. Varney unveiled new Seven Havens colorways for the full playable roster of Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, along with a new stage based on Sonam’s temple.

This news coincides with Avatar: Seven Havens getting renewed for two additional seasons, bringing the total to four. The first three episodes in season one premiered today, October 9 , on Paramount+, and three episodes will air weekly every Friday through October 30. At the time of writing, Book 2 does not yet have an official release date.

IGN's Alex Zalben reviewed the first three episodes of Seven Havens Book 1, which he scored a sparkling 9 out of 10 . "The first three episodes of the new Avatar are thrillingly emotional, beautifully animated, and stunningly scored. It’s great to have this world back, even if it is a broken post-apocalyptic version that’s perhaps not too far from our own," he wrote in our review.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month.

Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S.

Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below.

DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it.

The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone.

"There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'"

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Comic Book Icon Grant Morrison to Pen New James Bond Series for IDW Publishing
articles.summary: In what may well be the biggest comic book news out of NYCC, Grant Morrison has been tapped to write a new James Bond series for IDW Publishing.
articles.body:
In what may well be the biggest comic book-related news to come out of NYCC 2026, IDW Publishing has acquired the rights to publish new James Bond adventures. The company is turning to none other than legendary New X-Men and Doom Patrol writer Grant Morrison to launch a new ongoing James Bond series.

Few other details are known about the series right now, including the artist, official title, or release date. However, Morrison's name alone is ample cause for excitement.

We do know that Morrison's series will kick off with a six-part storyline dubbed "Sunbreaker." The writer teased their plans for the series in the following statement:

I’ve been a James Bond fan for as long as I can remember and this opportunity to put my own stamp on a British character as iconic as King Arthur, Robin Hood or Sherlock Holmes, was too good to miss.

Our opening 6-part adventure, Sunbreaker, attempts to create a definitive Bond story featuring everything fans love about the character and his world, while adding a whole lot more. Expect to see James Bond in a few unfamiliar situations, facing unfamiliar foes, in a world very like our own as reflected in a deadly funhouse mirror – a world of intrigue, violence, double cross and deception. A world through which James Bond glides like a killer shark among minnows. Charismatic, ruthless, unstoppable.

With new cars, new gadgets, and a terrifying new ultimate villain ripped straight from the headlines, get ready to be shaken and stirred, as James Bond faces the greatest challenge of his life in Sunbreaker!

This series marks the beginning of IDW's collaboration with Ian Fleming Publications Ltd. The James Bond license has found a home at several publishers over the decades, most recently at Dynamite Entertainment. You can check out IGN's review of 2015's James Bond #1 for more on that series.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Pretty Little Liars Star Keegan Allen Says He Was Robbed at Gunpoint in Bloody Video
articles.summary: Keegan Allen, best known for his role as Toby Cavanaugh in Pretty Little Liars, uploaded a shocking video to Instagram on the night of October 8, showing himself breathless and covered in blood.
articles.body:
Keegan Allen, known for his role as Toby Cavanaugh in Pretty Little Liars , uploaded a shocking video to Instagram on the night of October 8, showing himself breathless and covered in blood.

“I was just robbed of my watch outside of Laurel Supply,” Allen said, before turning away from the camera to ask someone to call the police. “These two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me, with a knife. They had masks on. They took my watch.”

Allen inserted CCTV footage from the incident taken by a nearby camera, which showed two men dressed in dark clothing approaching the actor near a truck. After Allen handed over his watch, one of the men struck him in the head twice, with both thieves quickly fleeing the scene.

In the caption of his Instagram post , Allen urged Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and California Governor Gavin Newsom to take action as the state's general election approaches.

“West Hollywood is not safe anymore,” he wrote. “Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said [not] tonight. My life for a watch. Will update more soon. Let’s hope all these flock cameras that @karenbassla @gavinnewsom and everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals. God bless.”

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's office published a statement about the crime that recounted the attack: "One suspect pointed a silver handgun at the victim while the other pointed a knife and demanded the victim's watch and bracelet. Shortly after, the victim was struck in the face with the handgun."

The crime took place at Laurel Supply, a high-end organic grocery store and market on 8445 Santa Monica Blvd. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and individuals with information about the incident are encouraged to contact authorities at the sheriff's West Hollywood station at (310) 855-8850.

Allen’s bloody video has gone viral, racking up over 135,000 likes in the hours since he posted it last night. Fans are showing up in droves to give their support to the actor, urging him to get checked for a possible concussion and many admitting to initially being mistaken that he was wearing makeup for a new project.

Allen is also known for portraying Liam Walker in the CW’s Walker , a reimagining of Chuck Norris’s Walker, Texas Ranger. Most recently, Allen played Ian Coleman in Season 8 of The Rookie .

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099: What Happens When the Replicants Are Running the World?
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with IGN, Blade Runner 2099 showrunner Silka Luisa says the new series will be an "undercover police story" that’s "quintessential Blade Runner."
articles.body:
So says Michelle Yeoh’s Olwen, one of the two leads of Prime Video’s upcoming series Blade Runner 2099 . Picking up 50 years (obviously) after Blade Runner 2049 , the dystopian future world that was first brought to the screen by Ridley Scott is in many ways the same in the show as it was in that 1982 film – vast cityscapes, flying cars, teeming masses, and big-as-hell shoulder pads.

But in other areas, things have changed significantly. Perhaps most notably, the Replicant underclass – androids designed by man as slave labor – have overtaken their human overseers after a war between the two races. Now it’s humankind that lives under the heel of the Replicants. And as Olwen says, it’s their time now…

In advance of Blade Runner 2099’s New York Comic Con panel on Saturday , we spoke to series creator Silka Luisa and production designer Paul Inglis about recreating the world first envisioned by Scott, and then Denis Villeneuve for Blade Runner 2049, and how channeling the Replicants versus humans dynamic – and the blurring of the line between the two groups that both films did so well – informed not only the design choices behind the new show, but also how the characters of Yeoh’s Olwen and Hunter Schafer’s Cora would take the latest chapter of Blade Runner to a new level.

An Undercover Cop Story… in a Dystopian Future

The Blade Runner films (and the 1968 book on which the original film was based, Philip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?) have always played with the idea of identity, be it the age-old question of whether or not Harrison Ford’s Rick Deckard is a Replicant, Ryan Gosling’s Agent K’s delusions of grandeur about being some kind of “chosen one,” or now, in 2099, Schafer’s Cora playing a human who is forced to pretend to be a Replicant Blade Runner… who, by the way, now hunt down rogue humans rather than Replicants. It seems to be getting harder than ever to tell the difference between human and Replicant.

“That's always been baked into the concept of the franchise – the idea that there could be something that looks just like us but is slightly other,” says Luisa. “And that is such an interesting, complicated character dynamic to explore. In our world, with the power dynamics flipped, it's also interesting to think, okay, what comes after us and do they have more right to be here than us at some point?”

There’s a moment in Episode 1 where a human says, “No one gets by me,” and a Replicant Blade Runner responds, “You’re human. Your whole world has already gone past you.” And indeed, that is the vibe of the show as things begin. Having lost the war between Replicants and humans at some point between the events of Blade Runner 2049 and this series, the humans now live in a world that not only did they ruin, but that the Replicants are trying to rebuild. Ecologically wrecked and polluted, Earth seems to have a shot once again at healing now that the Replicants can apply their terraforming skills from decades of off-world colony experience. A new life awaits you… on Earth!

This new status quo, which was seeded in Blade Runner 2049’s Replicant rebels, allows Luisa and her team to pay respect to what has come before in this universe but also chart new ground, as with the unlikely partnership between the Blade Runner Olwen and her new partner, Cora, who is essentially pulling a Matt Damon from The Departed. Forced to pretend to be a Replicant and a Blade Runner, she finds herself living a double life where she can trust virtually no one.

“It was important to be aware of and to respect the canon of the films in terms of historically what happens in them and the tentpole moments,” says Luisa. “The benefit of having this shift in status quo is that it's a new entry point for everyone, and that makes it accessible to new audiences and to fans because everyone is learning about this new world and the new dynamic and all the new characters.”

As for the idea of making Cora an undercover agent of sorts, Luisa points out that the films have always had an “investigatory police” element.

“Even though the world is fantastical and phenomenal and just stunning and surprising, there is a narrative engine that is familiar in a way that helps pull you through this very foreign world,” she explains. “And building on that, I was like, an undercover police story would be an interesting way to pair a Replicant and a human together and to figure out, can you tell an enemies to ally story within that structure?”

A key aspect of the show is also Yeoh’s character’s lifespan. Back in the original Blade Runner, the Replicants had four-year lifespans and then they shut down – died, actually. It seems Replicants get more time these days, but not enough, and Olwen is very aware that she is on her way out.

“This is the last week of her life,” says Luisa. “Blade Runner has always been about mortality. Part of the human experience is dying and it's inevitable, and Replicants know exactly when they're going to die, which in some ways makes it even harder because it's sooner than it should be. And that knowledge, I don't know if we're meant to have that. Can you ever stop fighting the desire to want to be here and to see how the story continues? That felt very fundamental.”

Re-Creating ‘Quintessential Blade Runner’ Tech for 2099

The spinners are certainly one of the most recognizable aspects of the Blade Runner world – the flying cars first conceived by the iconic designer Syd Mead for Ridley Scott’s original film. They carried through to Blade Runner 2049, and now they’re back once again for the new series. As Luisa says, they’re “quintessential Blade Runner.”

“Our [police] department spinners are intentionally quite muscular,” explains Paul Inglis, who served as supervising art director on Blade Runner 2049 and is now the production designer on the series. “They're intentionally quite industrial and quite harsh looking – maybe a nod to the fact that you want a sense of power to them, you want a sense that the people flying them come with muscularity, come with intent.”

“There's certain components of them that I don't think you can shift, because then they no longer are the Blade Runner you know and love,” says Luisa. “So what I really appreciated about Paul's design that he developed with George Hull was that it didn't stray so far from the films that you were no longer remembering the quintessential spinner. We talked a lot about them being heavier and having a weight to them. From the human perspective, Blade Runners are terrifying now and those Spinners arriving should feel like an undercover cop pulling up into your neighborhood where everyone knows who it is and you just scatter.”

Living in the actual Los Angeles also helped to inform how the future Los Angeles of the show should look, sound, and feel, and that included the sound of these spinners.

“I live in Los Angeles and something that really was startling when I first moved here was the sound of helicopters all the time,” says Luisa. “It's just something that is so unsettling, and in the sound design we talked a lot about. If you have these spinners that are police vehicles flying overhead, how do you give a sound to them that is just in your bones and it creates a sense of police state all the time?”

Says Inglis, “They very much were designed to [invoke] a ‘look at us, we're Blade Runners’ [feel] every time they land. There is a certain amount of trepidation that comes with seeing one of those flying through the air.”

It’s not just the spinners that are similar to their predecessors. Luisa and the rest of the team behind 2099 intentionally wanted to call back to the world of the original Blade Runner, which was set 80 years earlier in 2019, for story purposes.

“That came out of my initial conversations with Ridley,” says Luisa. “When you think of the show, it really is post-war. We're in the aftermath of this Replicant uprising and the city is no longer up and running in the same way it was in 2049. Manufacturing would've stopped. There would've been a regression in that sense. So we returned to the original aesthetic of the first film, much more so than 2049, where the idea is that the inner components that typically are hidden are visible and accessible. That was a design principle that he talks about a lot, was that everything on the inside is on the outside and it gives you a very analog and nostalgic feel, but from a practical sense it's actually incredibly useful because it's easier to repair things, it's easier to use components from different parts. And when thinking about the world, that made logical sense because these humans are scavenging from all different pockets of what they have left to assemble what they need now.”

“You have synthetic humans, you have flying cars, but some things are actually very set in the past,” says Inglis. “A lot of what we do to build this world is we look backwards to look forwards, but then we add things to that historical reference to bring them to a Blade Runner space. And I think that's what makes this distinct from a lot of other science fiction. It's almost like we have science fiction events, but in a non-science-fiction world in that our backdrop is tactile. It's tangible. It wants to feel as real as possible. And we're always trying to find materials, finishes and aging that gives the world a sense of [the viewer] wanting to reach out and touch it.”

Of course, considering the premise of this new iteration of Blade Runner, the question has to be asked: Can the Replicants really be the saviors of the future?

“In 2049, it felt like the environment was dying and there is a benefit – Replicants who had been terraforming and who had been building atmospheres on and off worlds, they can offer something to us in the sense that we could barely breathe our air and do they know how to rehabilitate it?” says Luisa. But there is another aspect to Earth’s new overlords as well.

“It's the idea of, they don't have childhoods, and so they don't develop empathy in the same way that we do. And then what would that do? How would that shift their worldview? How would you shape a city? How would you shape governance without that, without empathy?”

Blade Runner 2099 debuts on Prime Video on November 25.

Reporting by Jim Vejvoda and Amelia Emberwing

articles.title: Skate Developer Promises More Creative Tools Are Coming After ReSkate Modding Platform Goes Viral
articles.summary: Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.
articles.body:
Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.

ReSkate was officially released into the wild about a week ago. This platform allows fans to play the game offline, create private servers, make their own maps, and more. It’s already been downloaded over 350,000 times on GitHub, and its creators are well-aware that they might get hit with a cease-and-desist order.

However, that doesn’t seem to be a problem — at least, not yet, but the devs at Full Circle are keeping an eye on the situation. Full Circle published a statement acknowledging fan mods on October 9, where they admitted to the importance of community mods, while also standing firm against those that bypass paid cosmetics or make money off of new features.

“Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That's why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content,” it wrote.

“To be completely clear, we are not against creativity from players or stopping that from happening. Where we have to draw the line is when mods or other tools bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics, release gated/unreleased content, or profit from these unauthorized assets. That rips off the artists, skate brands, and creators, as well as our own development team here at Full Circle, who work hard to bring skate culture into our game."

Full Circle went on to confirm that it is aware that players want “more freedom and custom features,” and revealed that it’s currently building “official, secure access tools that enable broader, deeper community creation.” More news on this will be shared at a later date.

A message from the team at Full Circle regarding mods and community content. — skate. (@skate) October 9, 2026

A message from the team at Full Circle regarding mods and community content.

ReSkate’s popularity is undeniable; after its release, Skate’s playerbase saw a massive jump in active players, peaking at over 7,000 players on October 5 — the highest it’s been for months after the game's launch in September 2025.

Speaking with PC Gamer , the developers of ReSkate admitted that they “honestly didn't realize how big this was going to be," saying they were “just doing it for the love of the game."

They also told the outlet that they are prepared to take ReSkate down if EA’s lawyers come knocking, which many fans are already assuming will happen at some point down the line. For now, though, ReSkate remains alive and well, and it has seemingly spurred Full Circle into taking action to give the game more community-friendly features.

articles.title: Is Marvel's Zodiac Actually an Agents of SHIELD Revival?
articles.summary: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is expanding once again, because Marvel Studios has announced at New York Comic Con a new “spy thriller” called Zodiac. But could this actually be an Agents of SHIELD revival?
articles.body:
The Marvel Cinematic Universe is expanding once again, because Marvel Studios has announced at New York Comic Con another project that will debut after Avengers: Secret Wars wraps up the Multiverse Saga. That would be Zodiac , a new “spy thriller” from Marvel Television. But besides a 2028 release window, we don’t have any other official information beyond the show’s logo, which has resulted in Marvel fans the world over asking the question: What the heck is this show even about? Is it a character? An organization? Is Marvel making a TV series about the Zodiac Killer? (Not likely on that last one).

Meanwhile, Clark Gregg, aka Agent Phil Coulson from Agents of SHIELD , seems excited about the new show... or at least has shared the Zodiac news on social media. Hmm...

Well, Zodiac does in fact exist in the Marvel comics universe as a team of villains. So let’s look at the source material and other MCU projects to see if we can figure out what Marvel has up their sleeve... and whether or not this means Agents of SHIELD could somehow be returning too.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

The most prominent Zodiac in the Marvel universe is the Zodiac Cartel, a group of 12 supervillains who stylize themselves after the signs of Western astrology. So there’s someone named Aries, someone named Taurus, someone named Gemini... you get the idea. The organization is a subversive criminal group who sought world domination under the leadership of Cornelius van Lunt, aka Taurus, and would become recurring enemies of the Avengers. Although they made several appearances over the years, the Zodiac Cartel has never been a standout member of the Avengers’ rogues gallery – they’re not exactly on the same level as Loki, Ultron, or Thanos. Their schemes often involve the Zodiac Key, a powerful cosmic artifact that can generate psionic energy and empower mechanical devices.

One of the most notable aspects of the Zodiac Cartel is that Scorpio’s alter ego is Jake Fury, the brother of SHIELD director Nick Fury. While the original Zodiac stories had Jake as a villain who came into conflict with SHIELD and the Avengers, later stories in the Secret Warriors comic would reveal that the evil Jake was actually a Life Model Decoy (basically a robot that mimics a specific person), and the real Jake had been secretly helping his brother all along. The storyline in Secret Warriors also featured the Great Wheel, a version of the Zodiac group founded by none other than Leonardo da Vinci, which may be what's referenced in the "O" in the Zodiac show's logo.

Several other evil groups took up the Zodiac name after the first Cartel, including one composed entirely of Life Model Decoys, but none made much of an impact. Zodiac as a concept has struggled to break out in the Marvel comics universe, with other nefarious groups like Hydra, Advanced Idea Mechanics, and the Hand being much more popular.

Since Zodiac isn’t a well-known aspect of the Marvel universe, it’s surprising to see Marvel Studios greenlight a show named after them. It feels more likely that Marvel will reinvent the idea instead of doing a straightforward adaptation of the Zodiac Cartel – I doubt we’ll see van Lunt decked out in a bull costume. Since Hydra seems to be defunct in the MCU, and given that Marvel described the show as a spy thriller, perhaps Zodiac will be established as a new evil espionage group working in the shadows as part of the MCU’s next saga.

This would make sense given that the “A” in the Zodiac logo looks quite similar to the eagle emblem used for SHIELD in the MCU. Which raises our next question: Is Zodiac actually an Agents of SHIELD revival? That would track with Clark Gregg, who plays Phil Coulson in the MCU, sharing the Zodiac announcement on social media. Will the show feature the return of Agent Coulson? What about Chloe Bennet’s Quake or Ming-Na Wen’s Melinda May? It’s been a while since we’ve seen them, but the Agents of SHIELD characters making a comeback would be a welcome development for the MCU.

Agents of SHIELD is one of the holdouts from the pre-Disney+ era of Marvel television that hasn’t been reintegrated into the shared universe. Although Marvel Television insisted that “it’s all connected” back in the day, Coulson’s SHIELD team hasn’t been brought back in new MCU projects in the same way Daredevil and friends have. However, given that Zodiac has ties to SHIELD in the comics and the SHIELD insignia is referenced in the show’s logo, this feels like the perfect place for those characters to return to the fold. Perhaps Coulson’s team has to reunite to deal with a new threat in whatever form the MCU’s Zodiac organization takes. Maybe Samuel L. Jackson, who recently confirmed he will return as Nick Fury for Avengers: Secret Wars, will appear in Zodiac if they pursue the Jake Fury storyline.

Of course, we’d be remiss not to mention that Zodiac does already exist in one way in the MCU…

What About the Zodiac Bioweapon From Agent Carter?

So this is a deep cut even by MCU standards, but Marvel made a handful of short films called Marvel One-Shots in the MCU’s early days. One of those was Agent Carter in 2013, a precursor to the television show of the same name starring Hayley Atwell’s Peggy Carter.

In the short, which takes place after Steve Rogers went into the ice at the end of Captain America: The First Avenger, Peggy takes it upon herself to retrieve a blue vial from some criminals. This vial contains a bioweapon codenamed Zodiac, and while the short ends with Zodiac safely back in the good guys’ hands, it hasn’t been followed up on in later MCU projects. Could this bioweapon be what the bad guys are after in the Zodiac show? We don’t know, but it wouldn’t be the first time Marvel has picked up dangling plot threads many years down the line. Hopefully it works out better than the Leader’s appearance in Captain America: Brave New World!

What do you think Marvel’s Zodiac is about? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Lucasfilm Games Producer Responds After Galactic Racer Character Biddy Blas Goes Viral
articles.summary: If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.
articles.body:
If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.

It’s almost impossible to hate the guy, who tells you all about how awesome he is in a hilarious spiel that has somehow become everyone’s new vocal stim. In Huttese, Blas tells you: “Here’s a name for you, amateur! Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!”

However, it’s the fantastic voice acting behind this line that’s got players cracking up. “Biddy Blas! Scrib doon!” is an undeniable banger, and I personally cannot stop saying it in response to basically anything. (My poor friend group is already tired of it.)

This Star Wars: Galactic Racer voice acting though! 💀🤣 — NIB (@nib95_) October 6, 2026

This Star Wars: Galactic Racer voice acting though! 💀🤣

Posts of Blas introducing himself have gone viral on social media, to the point where they caught the attention of Lucasfilm Games Producer Craig Derrick, who responded to the overwhelming influx of love for Blas on Twitter/X.

“It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer!” he wrote. “Thank you for all the kind words! Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it.”

Biddy Blas is a Crocin who, as players have come to find out, will literally do whatever it takes to win… even if that means giving you a ‘gift’ that’s actually a bomb, which, if you accept it, will explode your ship and give your opponents a major head start.

It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer! Thank you for all the kind words! 🙏 Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it. 😂 — Craig Derrick (@craigderrick) October 7, 2026

It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer! Thank you for all the kind words! 🙏 Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it. 😂

Hate him or love him, the guy’s the talk of the town right now, with some fans affectionately dubbing him the “glup shitto of the year.”

“I would like to say I'd die for Biddy Blas, but at the same time, I have also slammed him into a wall at like 500mph multiple times at this stage,” one fan joked .

“Biddy Blas is hilarious, I'm going to kill him,” another said after their speeder got blown up thanks to accepting Blas’s ‘gift.’

Star Wars: Galactic Racer - June 2026 Screenshots

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been a major hit with Star Wars fans and critics alike, with IGN’s Luke Reilly scoring the game an 8 out of 10. “Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that gets a little repetitive thanks to its heavy reliance on repeatedly revisiting the same slim selection of planets, but has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe,” he wrote in our review .

It’s a good time to be a pod racer, as developer Fuse Games recently announced that Galactic Racer’s multiplayer party limit will soon double in size in a post-launch patch coming in the next few weeks.

It keeps a very similiar design as the lauded R1S but shrinks both the size and the price. The R2's base price is $45,000, though in this current early stage of production, only the maxed-out, tri-motor, fully loaded Performance model is available for a starting price of $58,000.

articles.summary: Marvel dropped some big announcements at NYCC, including Daredevil #700 and a brand-new Captain Marvel series from Kamala Khan co-creator G. Willow Wilson.
articles.body:
Marvel Comics made some big announcements during the publisher's "Bullpen Bulletins! With Stephen Wacker" panel. The newly minted editor-in-chief revealed several big projects for early 2027, including a brand-new ongoing Captain Marvel series and the milestone issue Daredevil #700.

The new volume of Captain Marvel will be written by G. Willow Wilson, whom Marvel fans will best remember as the co-creator of current Ms. Marvel Kamala Khan. This time, Wilson is turning her attention to Kamala's mentor, Carol Danvers, who is facing a dark new status quo following the destructive events of Avengers: Armageddon .

Captain Marvel will be illustrated by Rachael Stott (Fantastic Four). Here's the official summary for the series:

Following the cataclysmic events of Avengers: Armageddon, Carol Danvers finds herself grounded like never before. To rise again, Carol will have to challenge everything she thought she knew about being Captain Marvel—and break every rule along the way. And as she pushes herself further, a threat that has been quietly assembling in the shadows of the Marvel Universe for decades is finally ready to make its move.

Look for Captain Marvel #1 to debut in May 2027.

As for Daredevil, the series will reach its 700th issue in March 2027. That oversized issue will feature a main story by regular series writer Stephanie Phillips and artist Lee Garbett, along with a new cover by Daredevil veteran David Mack.

Also during the panel, Marvel teased the climactic finale of a major Uncanny X-Men storyline called "Soul Deep," as well as a spinoff miniseries called X-Men: Regulators. Regulators is written by Mikki Kendall and drawn by Georges Jeanty and will debut in February 2027. You can see covers for these and the other books featured in the panel below:

articles.title: The Street Fighter 2 Bonus Stage Car Is Real and You Can Win It
articles.summary: The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money.
articles.body:
The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money.

Street Fighter II’s iconic bonus stage lets players beat the literal brakes off of a Lexus LS 400. It’s a feature that’s stayed with the series throughout the years, challenging fighting game fans to beat it to a pulp within a certain time limit.

It’s even referenced in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, with trailers showing Noah Centineo’s Ken Masters punching and kicking a car to bits while surrounded by a crowd of adoring fans.

More than 30 years later, this car is coming to the real world, thanks to a joint collaboration between The General Insurance (yes, that General), Capcom, and Vehicle Effects, a Los Angeles-based company that makes custom rides of all sorts, many of which have been featured in films and TV shows.

Vehicle Effects has made a recreation of the pixelated Lexus from Street Fighter II — though we don’t recommend you actually destroy it if you end up winning it in their sweepstakes. Starting in October, fans have until November 18 to enter the sweepstakes for a chance at snagging the car for themselves, as well as $25,400.69 (nice) in gas money.

And hey, it’s a pretty good car; as pointed out by Eventhubs , the Lexus LS 400 is widely considered to be one of the most “overengineered” cars of all time, with a 4.0-liter V8 engine that’s been nicknamed the "million-mile engine.” (It’s the only thing left behind after you destroy it in the bonus stage, after all.)

On top of its pixelated paint job and upgraded sound system, the words “you” and “win” are emblazoned on both the driver’s side and passenger side headrests, and you can even insert a literal coin to activate its accompanying seat warmers. It’s hard to kick butt when you’ve got cold glutes, after all.

The Street Fighter movie releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. Just today, it was revealed that the movie will feature animated segments diving into Ryu and Ken’s backstory with their master, Gouken, and Akuma. We got the chance to speak to the cast of the film ahead of time, including David Dastmachian, who told us all about how he studied real-life cult leaders to bring M. Bison to the big screen .

Fans of the iconic dinosaur hunter Turok will be pleased to know the character is making a big comeback at Skybound in 2027. As announced at NYCC, the company is kicking off a new creator-focused imprint called Skybound Visions, one that launches with a Turok: Son of Stone comic and new additions to the Transformers and G.I. Skybound Visions is intended to offer standalone stories focused on creators reinventing popular characters in bold and unexpected ways. Case in point, Turok: Son of Stone reboots the character under The Buffalo Hunter Hunter writer Stephen Graham Jones and The Old Guard artist Leandro Fernández.

“Skybound Visions pairs beloved comic book characters with the most interesting comic book creators working today, to present their personal takes on these fan-favorites,” said Sean Mackiewicz, SVP, Skybound, in a statement. “Visions is all about surprising creators, surprising characters, and surprising storytelling, and we have plenty more in store for 2027 and beyond."

Read on to learn more about all three of the inaugural Skybound Visions titles and see early previews of each one.

But on this island, survival isn’t just half the battle--it's the whole damn war!

Turok wanted to dig up the past. Now, he must survive it. Turok dreamed that his dig in New Mexico would make his name legendary. But when the ground gave way, he fell through history and landed in a valley that shouldn’t exist. Where the Ice Age sits on top of the time of dinosaurs, and at every turn he discovers an era older and hungrier than the last. In a relentless quest to return to his son, Turok must unearth the truth about this hidden world and not lose his grip on a shifting reality that threatens to consume him. Sometimes a dream coming true is a nightmare beyond imagination…

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Estimated Sales Reach Just 230,000 in First Week, Analyst Says
articles.summary: Xbox console exclusive Gears of War: E-Day is reportedly off to a soft start after reaching an estimated 230,000 copies sold in its first week.
articles.body:
Xbox console exclusive Gears of War: E-Day is reportedly off to a soft start after reaching an estimated 230,000 copies sold in its first week.

The alleged sales update arrived from Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, who shared early data for the Gears prequel on X/Twitter. After arriving via early access last week (its full launch arrived this past Tuesday), Gears of War: E-Day has reportedly moved just 230,000 copies across PC and Xbox devices.

Steam sales account for 168,000 of that number, with Xbox sales, including both console and PC, totaling just 62,000. These numbers, which are unofficial figures that have not been backed by Microsoft in any official capacity and should be taken with a grain of salt, are low for the game leading the charge on Xbox's refocus toward exclusive games, as players shift their attention from purchasing the base experience to dipping their toes in with Game Pass.

Game Pass is seemingly to blame for its performance related to raw copies sold on Xbox-supported devices, with Elliott saying the subscription service is "cannibalising much of the premium revenue." While that's not to say Gears of War: E-Day is having trouble garnering attention – Alinea estimated that 1.7 million players have accessed the game via Game Pass – the data does suggest that players are far more interested in access through their subscriptions rather than outright owning a copy.

Of the nearly 2 million to launch Gears of War: E-Day through Game Pass, 722,000 users are believed to have paid the extra $30 to upgrade to its Premium Edition to unlock early access. Revenue earned through the Xbox ecosystem reportedly amounted to $27 million, with total earnings reaching about $37 million. How exactly Gears of War: E-Day may have factored into revenue earned through new and returning Game Pass subscriptions is currently unclear.

"While E-Day is a sublime game (it's made my top 10), these are soft numbers for a flagship when Xbox badly needs revenue wins," Elliott said. "E-Day sold 62K copies on Xbox against 722K Premium upgrades, so for every one copy sold on Xbox, nearly 12 Game Pass upgrades were sold. The $70 premium SKU is – functionally – dead on Xbox. In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70. They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don’t own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration."

Gears of War: E-Day Gameplay Demo Reveal Xbox Games Showcase 2026 - Screenshots

The idea that Game Pass has negatively affected standalone sales is something Microsoft has seemingly been internally aware of before, with 2023 documents related to the Activision Blizzard merger noting a decline in base game sales in the first year after a title is added to the service. The Xbox company told IGN at the time that the model "offers gamers and game creators more choice and opportunity in how they discover, experience, and deliver games."

While Microsoft has yet to confirm official sales data, and it's unclear how Gears of War: E-Day may have driven new Game Pass subscriptions, slow sales could sour an otherwise successful launch. The Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago-led prequel emerged with strong reviews from both fans and critics, with IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, awarding a 9/10 .

Earlier this week, The Coalition studio head Mike Crump said Gears of War: E-Day is a "natural choice to be" an Xbox exclusive . He also addressed concerns around potential layoffs at the studio , while promising that the next installment in the series won't take nearly as long to make.

articles.title: Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
articles.summary: Price hikes have made DDR5 RAM so expensive that chipmakers are launching new CPUs for older platforms running on DDR4 RAM.
articles.body: CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs. Their solution? A return to last-gen DDR4 RAM. Intel and AMD are making new CPUs that’ll support the older, more affordable type of memory. On Friday, Gigabyte announced that two of its motherboard lines will support “upcoming” processors built on Intel’s LGA 1700 socket. That socket debuted in 2021 with the 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and supported both DDR4 RAM and the then-new DDR5 RAM. Intel dropped it for a DDR5-only approach in 2024. But according to Gigabyte, the dual format support is now being revived, with new LGA 1700 chips “expected to launch in early 2027.” Intel did not immediately respond to a request for comment. This backtrack stems from LGA 1700’s cross-compatibility with both kinds of RAM — an advantage over its successor that’s recently become much more important. Intel’s strategy may be to offer users the choice of a new CPU that doesn’t require them to switch to new, and very expensive, DDR5 memory, too. AMD is doing something similar: in August, Gigabyte also announced a new series of motherboards for AMD’s last-gen, DDR4-compatible AM4 platform to go along with the 10th-anniversary relaunch of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU. DDR4 started hitting the market in 2014 and has since been succeeded by the much faster DDR5. Under normal circumstances, buying new hardware to use technology that’s over a decade old would probably be a bad investment. But the RAM shortage is changing the math, with DDR4 RAM seemingly feeling the sting of price hikes much less than DDR5. I recently saw the price disparity first-hand while shopping around for new RAM after a DDR4 kit abruptly died on me. Right now, a DDR5 32GB Corsair Vengeance RAM kit costs $620, while the corresponding DDR4 kit costs $260. Even though it’s more than 32GB of DDR4 RAM typically cost back in mid-2025, that’s more than double the price for DDR5! Of course, DDR5 has significant advantages, like higher speeds and better power efficiency. But those perks might not be worth the current price of admission. It could be years before prices drop again, a reality that’s starting to really sink in with the official return of older sockets and chipsets. But at least it’s a good time to hang onto your DDR4 RAM.

articles.title: The Oregon Coast Aquarium Has Now Named Multiple Octopuses After Dungeon Crawler Carl Characters
articles.summary: The influence of Dungeon Crawler Carl has officially reached the animal kingdom. The Oregon Coast Aquarium just welcomed a new giant Pacific Octopus and named it after a certain changeling that fans of the series will recognize: Juicebox.
articles.body:
The influence of Dungeon Crawler Carl has officially reached the animal kingdom. The Oregon Coast Aquarium just welcomed a new giant Pacific Octopus and named it after a certain changeling that fans of the series will recognize: Juicebox.

While it's certainly interesting that Matt Dinniman's characters have already taken root in my local aquarium, according to the report from Oregon Live , this is actually the second Octopus to get named after DCC. Juicebox will be sharing the aquarium with a 22.5-pound male Octopus called Donut, after Princess Donut herself.

The aquarists who chose Juicebox's name told Oregon Live it was because of octopuses' inherent ability to change their appearance to blend in. For those not familiar with the books, Juicebox is a changeling that is able to shift into various forms at will. For additional context (and minor spoiler!), Juicebox does shift into Ursula from The Little Mermaid at one point in the story, so the transition to an octopus isn't that big of a stretch.

Juicebox the Octopus is now available to visit at the Oregon Coast Aquarium in Newport and will stay there for about a year before being released back to the reef. As someone who has regularly visited that aquarium, I can attest to the quality of their Octopus Den. And as a fan of the Dungeon Crawler Carl books , this little tidbit of news is a great excuse to go back and visit again.

Naming an octopus after a character from a popular franchise is certainly just a marketing stunt to get more people to visit the aquarium, but that doesn't make it any less impactful. The fact that Juicebox got added to the aquarium just as another octopus named Anakin was released just makes it even better. Will Dungeon Crawler Carl ever be as big as Star Wars? Probably not, but the octopus trends seem to be heading in that direction.

The sudden rise from popular LitRPG book series to octopus fame is par for the course for Dungeon Crawler Carl in 2026. This year alone, the eighth book is coming out — along with tabletop games and an entire toy line — and a TV adaptation was confirmed at Peacock with Seth McFarlane in charge.

With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.body:
Earlier this year at MagicCon in Las Vegas, Wizards of the Coast revealed its in-universe sets for 2027, but that only covered three of the six planned sets. articles.title: Rays wait for ALCS opponent after winning 101 games playing any brand of baseball needed to win
articles.summary: (AP) — The Tampa Bays Rays showed they can play any brand of baseball during a sweep of the New York Yankees.They mixed power from likely and unlikely source...
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — The Tampa Bays Rays showed they can play any brand of baseball during a sweep of the New York Yankees.

They mixed power from likely and unlikely sources and their usual small-ball style along with dominant pitching, excellent fielding and strong fundamentals.

That was the formula that led to 98 wins in the regular season, three more against the Yankees and has the Rays waiting for their opponent in the AL Championship Series.

Tampa Bay faces either the Cleveland Guardians or Chicago White Sox. Game 5 of that series is Saturday night.

"I think what the guys have done so incredibly well is shown the ability to kind of adjust on the fly and some of that is reactive," manager Kevin Cash said Friday. "Like, we got a starter that's rolling against us or some tough matchups for us, to have the ability to shift gears and say, alright, we're gonna see if we can get a leadoff runner on or get a guy at second base and move him over, or we put pressure on the defense when you got a high strikeout guy on the mound and there's a guy at third with less than two outs and put pressure on the pitcher, the defense to drop a bunt down.

"I don't overlook that at all. I think that's who we are. And, there are some nights that we're gonna need to go out and slug with the opponent, but there are some nights that we're gonna do everything we can to just scratch and claw to get a run across the board."

Drew Rasmussen was so dominant in the series opener against New York that Jonathan Aranda's solo homer was all the support needed.

But the Rays' pesky style of putting the ball in play, moving runners over, using their speed and taking advantage of mistakes was the difference in Game 2. The Yankees fell apart defensively and Tampa Bay made them pay for it in a 5-2 win.

The Rays finished off New York with a 4-3 victory on Wednesday behind homers from Victor Mesa Jr. and Ryan Vilade – two guys who went deep a combined 25 times in the regular season.

The Rays were David against the Goliath Yankees, who opened the season with MLB's third-highest payroll at $303 million to $91 million for Tampa Bay.

The players weren't paying attention to that disparity.

"We don't care, and I think that's an ultimate credit to our players," Cash said. "They don't focus on that. They come in day in, day out doing whatever they can to help us win a game that night. So I respect that it's talked about throughout the industry, but ultimately, it comes down to having really good players that came together this season and have found multiple ways to win games."

They'll face a team with an even smaller payroll in the ALCS. The Guardians had the lowest opening day 40-man payroll this year at $75.5 million and the White Sox had the third-lowest payroll to start the season.

The Rays were 4-2 this year against the White Sox and 5-1 versus Cleveland. They will have played just three games in 14 days before the ALCS opener at Tropicana Field on Monday night.

"They've had a great series, know that they're two very talented teams, excited to watch how that's going to unfold (Saturday) night," Cash said.

Cash wouldn't name Rasmussen his Game 1 starter, though the All-Star right-hander is the obvious choice. He took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Yankees and will be on eight days' rest.

articles.title: A Street Fighter Movie Sequel Is Already Being Written, but There’s a Catch
articles.summary: Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs.
articles.body:
Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs.

Sakurai spoke about the possibility of a sequel in an interview with MovieWeb , saying the groundwork is already being laid to continue Ryu and Ken’s adventures after the events of the second World Warrior Tournament. But if fans want to see their fights continue after this, they’ll have to put their butts in some seats at their local theaters to make it happen.

“It's something that we're thinking about and developing,” he told the outlet. “I don't want to say anything that locks us in. It also kind of depends on how people react to this one, and whether they, you know, support this vision of the story. We definitely have a lot of ideas, and we're writing currently, but you know, I wouldn't want to make any promises one way or the other about what exactly we're gonna do."

Having spoken with the cast myself, I can confirm that their hopes for a sequel are high, but they’ve also confirmed that interest from moviegoers is essential in order to justify making another Street Fighter film.

Just today, it was confirmed that the Street Fighter movie will contain several animated sequences diving into Ryu and Ken’s backstory with their mentor, Gouken, and his brother, Akuma. Fans are already providing positive feedback to what they’ve seen so far, praising the art style and fluid animation — but there’s one character who’s been left out of the marketing thus far, and he’s already getting the community’s gears turning as to who a sequel might be about.

We haven’t yet seen Sagat in any of the film's trailers or advertisements, and no casting announcements have been made for him. Obviously, fans are hopeful that, if a sequel does end up getting made, Sagat will be a significant part of it — but given the wealth of characters in Street Fighter games , there’s no telling who might show up in a second movie.

This is the second big film from Capcom to hit theaters following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil adaptation, which was broadly well-received by regular moviegoers and critics, alike, though hopes for a sequel are also low at the moment, given that Cregger has publicly claimed he will "never" touch a franchise film again.

Street Fighter releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. We got the chance to speak to the cast ahead of its release, including David Dastmalchian, who told us all about how he studied real-life cult leaders to bring M. Bison to the big screen.
