articles.title: Guardians' Gavin Williams to start vs. White Sox's Sean Burke in winner-take-all ALDS Game 5
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — After pitching the ninth inning Thursday night, Gavin Williams will get the start for the Cleveland Guardians in Saturday night's winner-tak...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — After pitching the ninth inning Thursday night, Gavin Williams will get the start for the Cleveland Guardians in Saturday night's winner-take-all Game 5 of their AL Division Series against Sean Burke and the Chicago White Sox.

"Gavin wants the ball. We want him to have the ball, and it's his game," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said after announcing Williams was his starter.

Williams was the eighth Cleveland pitcher used during Thursday night's 9-5 win in Game 4 at Chicago. He made his first relief appearance in the majors on Thursday after reliever Cade Smith got into trouble in the ninth after Miguel Vargas homered and Munetaka Murakami drew a walk.

The right-hander threw 18 pitches with one hit allowed and one strikeout to nail down the win and even the best-of-five series at two games apiece.

Williams said he walked by Vogt's office after the game and told the third-year manager he was ready to go.

"The body feels good right now. I've been in the training room all morning, just figuring it out. But it's just a normal day really," said Williams, who went 14-8 during the regular season and led the AL with 248 strikeouts. I throw a pen on those days and everybody knows it. So there's nothing different. Just being able to feel the mound in a game situation is even better at that point."

Williams struck out 11 in five-plus innings in Monday's 4-3 loss in Game 2 . He was the first pitcher in franchise history to whiff five straight in a postseason game. He also had 16 pitches over 100 mph, the fourth-most by an AL pitcher in a playoff game since tracking started in 2008.

The 27-year old Williams allowed two runs on four hits. He threw 98 pitches, including 59 strikes, but got into trouble by allowing the leadoff hitter to get aboard in the fourth, fifth and sixth innings. The Guardians had a 2-0 lead before the White Sox rallied with three in the sixth to take the lead.

This will be Williams' sixth start and seventh appearance against the White Sox this season. He is 0-1 with a 3.76 ERA with 40 strikeouts and 11 walks.

"They're still a hard team to pitch to. There's nothing really to learn at this point of the season. I know what they got, and they know what I got," Williams said.

Burke will be making his fifth appearance and third start against Cleveland this year and is 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA.

The right-hander came in during the third inning of Monday's game and earned the win. He retired 13 straight batters at one point while allowing one run on one hit with six strikeouts.

"I think I did a pretty good job of commanding all my stuff in the zone. I think that's kind of the key with this team. You see the last couple games how they were able to piece together bigger innings when you're not as sharp with command, or you get behind guys, you walk guys, and then this team kind of thrives," Burke said.

It is the first time in seven games this postseason the White Sox will go with a traditional starter. Burke said manager Will Venable approached him on Wednesday about that scenario.

"Sean is someone that's going to play a big role in tomorrow's game as the bulk guy. As we kind of evaluated the set of guys that we have and that we'll use tomorrow, it made sense to start him," Venable said.

It will be an all hands on deck situation for both teams with the winner heading to Tampa Bay for Game 1 of the AL Championship Series on Monday.

Chicago has a 9-8 advantage in games this season, but Cleveland was able to win its third straight AL Central title by one game, which gave the Guardians home field for this series.

However, home field hasn't meant much since the road team has won all four games.

"We would obviously have loved to win Game 3 or 4. There's been a couple of times that Vogter and I have just looked at each other and laughed because this is just how it goes with these two clubs. And I think it's a special thing," Venable said. "If you look at just the story of the battle that we've had with these guys throughout this season coming down to that last weekend for the division and then here we are with a Game 5 for a chance to go to the CS, I think it's fitting two really good clubs that are both just very competitive, really talented, and the heart and soul of the club and identity of the club comes through, and I think it's been cool to watch that play out in competition throughout the year."

NEW YORK (AP) — Allisha Gray will miss Game 3 of the Atlanta Dream's semifinal series with the New York Liberty on Friday night.

Gray injured her left hand in the best-of-five series opener and missed Wednesday night's Game 2. She briefly returned in Game 1 after going to the locker room, but went down a second time after diving for a loose ball and did not return.

The team's leading scorer went through warmups with black tape on her last two fingers on her shooting hand before Friday's game, but was ruled out about an hour before the tip. Gray looked good in warmups, hitting numerous 3-pointers and free throws.

"They came back and said Lish was out today," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said pregame. "She's making good progress since her injury. In the interest of caution, they ruled her out for today."

Atlanta leads the series 2-0 and will look to close it out Friday.

articles.title: Is The Exorcist: Martyrs a Sequel to The Exorcist III? Mike Flanagan Reveals All
articles.summary: The Exorcist: Martyrs director Mike Flanagan joins IGN to break down the horror sequel's new trailer and explain how it builds on the foundation of The Exorcist III.
articles.body:
There's a lot to be excited about at this year's NYCC, not least of which being the first trailer for Mike Flanagan's The Exorcist: Martyrs . The previous attempt at reinvigorating this iconic horror franchise didn't go so well, but if anyone can turn the ship around, it's the man behind The Haunting of Hill House and the new Carrie series.

IGN's Tom Jorgensen was able to sit down with Flanagan and take a deep dive into the trailer. Flanagan breaks down the key characters seen in this new footage and how the film builds on the foundation of the underrated gem that is The Exorcist III. Check out our video interview above or read on to see what he had to say about the film, including the all-important question of whether or not we'll hear "Tubular Bells" in the new film.

Tom Jorgensen for IGN: [Let's start with] the first shot of the trailer, which is Scarlett [Johansson] coming down the stairs into that crime scene. Explain why that was the image that you wanted to come right out of the gate with for this trailer.

Mike Flanagan: So when we were filming that, we had this incredible location. And I mean, if you're talking about The Exorcist and you have a staircase like that, it's kind of a requirement for a genre like this. That image, I think, not only evokes the descent of Scarlett's character into our story in a really profound way, but is also so evocative to me of the stairs from the original film and of the poster. If you look at the poster for The Exorcist III, check out that poster against that shot. It's kind of wild.

IGN: You mentioned The Exorcist III, and you've hinted prior to this that this movie is going to be taking some cues from that sequel. And I think you were maybe understating that a little bit from watching this trailer. What was so appealing about using The Exorcist III as the jumping-off point for this story?

Flanagan: The Exorcist III is an awesome movie. It's so underappreciated. Outside of the original, it's my favorite of the franchise. I think it's just a marvelous film. It's terrifying, it's sophisticated, it's beautifully acted. And the thing is that Blatty, both in the novel Legion on which it's based, and then in the film which he directed, is starting to play with the synthesis of two subgenres. And I think that's where I was like, "Aha, what a phenomenal idea. And there's so much we can do to take that idea and run with it." To harmonize a serial killer investigative thriller with the demonic possession story is something that I think that movie first tries to introduce and gives us a chance to truly run with, and that was irresistible.

IGN: Yeah, I'll tell you, I figured it was going to be relevant. I had actually not seen The Exorcist III before this weekend, and I just had something itching at me saying it was going to be relevant and that was a good investment of my time. And you're right, the movie is incredible.

IGN: This trailer is littered with references to the Gemini Killer. We have crucified victims, victims being mutilated in quite specific ways. What is this movie's relationship to the events of The Exorcist III? Do you consider this a direct sequel?

Flanagan: Well, it's a tricky question. I think this movie was absolutely designed to stand on its own two feet with people like yourself a week ago who had not seen The Exorcist III. So it is absolutely a self-contained story that is utterly accessible and hopefully thrilling for people who have no knowledge of The Exorcist III, or even frankly of Friedkin's film or Blatty's original novel. It really is its own thing.

However, that said, if you are a fan of The Exorcist III, there's just extra bits in here that will delight you. And there is a thread for the super fans to pick up that runs all the way back through the Exorcist III to Friedkin's original for those who are excited by those things. But it was absolutely crafted very intentionally to stand on its own.

IGN: Well, I'm going to be one of those people freakishly pulling at those threads for sure. A centerpiece moment of the trailer is Scarlett's character attending the execution of Rivera, who is played by John Leguizamo — incredible casting there by the way — surrounded by hooded executioners. That hood is a motif that recurs throughout the back half of the trailer. What can you tease about Rivera and his significance to this story?

Flanagan: Rivera is a serial killer who would leave crime scenes with a very particular religious tableau. Scarlett comes across him very early in the story, and it starts her career as a detective to close that case and to send him away to kind of a final justice. But then elements of that case and of his crime scenes begin to recur in a way that is a bit impossible, that goes beyond what would be possible for a simple copycat. And this case comes back into her life more than a decade later, now that she's a fully established homicide detective and a single mother, and it all kind of comes together.

IGN: I'll just say this: I've never paid more attention to which finger of a victim's was severed in a trailer than I have in this trailer right here. We see Scarlett chasing an orange-hooded character out of her house with a gun. Clearly this evil is starting to encroach. Does that theme have a relevance to what you're doing here, the idea of evil coming inside?

Flanagan: I think that's kind of at the very heart of every possession story, the incursion of evil onto the human heart, and in this case the human body, into the safety of the family and into innocence itself. That's some of what is fundamentally disturbing about an exorcist story. But the other difference is that the incursion of evil upon society, the incursion of violence upon a civilized world, and how that inspires despair in us when we see the evils of the world and the atrocities with which people can deal with each other — how that despair is something that we can't really escape. And once that infiltrates us, how do you get rid of that? The interesting thing about the synthesis of these two subgenres for me is that typically our protagonists in stories like this react in paralyzed horror to that incursion.

Scarlett's character does not have that luxury. She's a homicide detective. She is eye to eye with the greatest horrors that humans can inflict upon each other on a regular basis, and so it is her job — to that scene you're describing in the trailer — to chase down that evil, to run right toward it, to run headfirst into the darkness. [That's] another thing I love about that image of her at the staircase, because that's a moment of observation before you know she's going down there. That's her mission, her job, and it's also who she is, and that makes for a wonderful protagonist that gets to drive this narrative into a lot of places a lot of other possession stories can't go, because there's stories of people running from the darkness, whereas ours is running into it.

IGN: It seems like there are also two priests that are going to be allied with Scarlett, very appropriate for The Exorcist, played by Chiwetel Ejiofor and Laurence Fishburne. Holy hell.

Flanagan: I know, right? A lot of power in that room.

IGN: Excellent voices to be potentially booming some ancient rites. What can you tell us about these two priests?

Flanagan: Well, I can tell you Chiwetel plays a character named Father William, who's a prison chaplain, which I think is a fascinating look into a corner of the priesthood that is not really shown before in this franchise or in other Exorcist movies that I could find or think of. When you talk about the level of evil we're dealing with — and I've said before, I truly believe this is the scariest movie I've ever gotten to work on by quite a lot — there's a profound darkness. There's an epistle darkness at the heart of this story and it is vicious. This is a story about the fight against that kind of darkness. And if you're going to be depicting that fight, you need fighters of a certain weight. And when you talk about Laurence Fishburne, this is someone who carries that weight with him the second he steps into a room in a way that is pretty profound. So yeah, there's a bit of a heavyweight matchup here.

IGN: I think my favorite performance of Chiwetel Ejiofor's ever is actually The Operative in Serenity, that almost religious, dogmatic appreciation for something. Was that role at all on your mind when you cast him?

Flanagan: Oh, I love that movie so much. I geeked out on him when we did Life of Chuck about Serenity, and particularly there's one line in this beautiful high-angle shot at the end where he says, "There's nothing left to see." It's a haunting sign-off for this true believer that is so misguided. It's a wonderful character. But yeah, I think Chiwetel's an extraordinary actor, one of the best I've ever worked with. And that's why after we did Life of Chuck, I was determined to work with him again. But this part lets him do a number of things that'll be very surprising.

Flanagan: Yeah, it's a wonderful role for him and I think one of my favorite of his performances.

IGN: There's this really excellent image that I loved of this bloody barrel in that abandoned mall. It gets paid off later in very gory fashion. What do you notice most about how both The Exorcist and The Exorcist III evoke terror, and how do you go about honoring that in this movie with imagery like that?

Flanagan: Well, I think the thing that terrified me the most about The Exorcist — and there are visceral scares throughout, images, sounds, things that hit you on this primal level — isn't the rotating heads or the vomit or the levitation. The thing that scares me about The Exorcist is that it paints a portrait of a world where Satan is clearly real and active and God seems nowhere to be found. And that chills me. There's no safety net. It's a world where innocent children can die horribly and no God will intervene on their behalf, which coincidentally is the world we live in. I think that is at its heart what makes it so upsetting, and I think where these films and the books especially tap into something that I think really affects people is that it roots this in a perversion of religious iconography.

It takes things that are meant to be sacred and makes them a sacrilege. That barrel, if you have a certain level of knowledge of the method of death of Catholic saints and martyrs, means something and it's a twisted perversion of something that is holy in the church. As someone who was raised Catholic and who was horrified and fascinated by martyrdom and by the method of death of so many Catholic saints — which are, I have to say, some of the worst ways you can imagine a human being dying in a lot of cases — to imagine a mockery of that where there appears to be no safety net and no intervention from anything good regardless of the nature of the victim made the story horrifying to me. That's what terrifies me about it. There's scares, there's imagery, there's all sorts of stuff that's truly unsettling, but the thing that unsettles me the most is unchecked evil in the human world that there appears to be no remedy for. That to me is just horrifying.

articles.title: Blumhouse Partners With MatPat to Make Amanda the Adventurer Movie, Confirms More Indie Horror Game Adaptations Are Coming | NYCC 2026
articles.summary: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket.
articles.body:
Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket.

Representatives from Blumhouse and MatPat confirmed this partnership at New York Comic Con 2026, where they said the YouTuber has “a few projects in the works” with the studio.

“I am proud to announce that I’m working with Blumhouse to launch some new movies. I am taking some of my all-time favorite indie games and horror channels from the interwebs and partnering with Blumhouse to bring them to the big screen,” MatPat said at the panel.

The first of these is Amanda the Adventurer, a first-person, puzzle-solving indie horror game that sees the player character unravel an unsettling mystery involving a low-budget animated children’s show of the same name.

MatPat announced that he and Blumhouse are currently in talks with writers and directors, saying they’re “actually moving fast” to get this project made.

“It’s horror with heart. Amanda is this horrifying but tragic character. It asks the question, ‘Can you trust the media being put in front of your kids?’” he said.

This is the latest YouTuber-led film project to hit the news after Sean ‘Jacksepticeye’ McLoughlin revealed he was at the helm of an animated Bloodborne movie . And earlier this year, YouTube star Mark ‘Markiplier’ Fischbach stunned moviegoers with his self-funded horror movie Iron Lung , an adaptation of an indie horror game of the same name.

Indie horror games have always had a strong audience online, and it seems that major studios are finally taking notice — especially after the success of Kane Parson’s Backrooms earlier this year. The film was such a hit that other creepypasta movies were greenlit in short order, including adaptations of The Mandela Catalogue , Siren Head , and even The SCP Foundation.

Given the viral nature of Amanda the Adventurer, there’s a few good guesses as to what movies MatPat and Blumhouse are cooking up next. Probably all one needs to do is look at CoryxKenshin’s YouTube channel — could a Puppet Combo movie be on the way? (Nun Massacre would be wild to see in a theater.)

For more New York Comic Con news, check out our hub of everything major announced at the convention's Marvel panel, as well as a new Avatar: The Last Airbender show and our interview with Daredevil star Charlie Cox.

articles.title: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
articles.summary: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.
articles.body:
Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.

Okamoto offered a foggy glimpse into the classic horror franchise's future during an interview featured in Famitsu Issue 1965 (via Game Observer ). The series ended a long, painful drought without new games with an initial wave of new releases over the last few years, and now that this first batch is out, Konami is already looking forward to what it can do next.

"All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we’re relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They’ve also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it."

Okamoto continued: "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we’re not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can’t share specific details, but we’re currently looking at a number of projects."

The first wave of Konami's return to Silent Hill – which included titles like the Silent Hill 2 remake , Silent Hill f , and last month's Silent Hill: Townfall – rolled out throughout the last few years. Townfall arrived as the most recent installment when it dropped players into the shoes of protagonist Simon Ordell in a '90s Scotland just last month.

It received generally favorable reviews, with IGN giving it an 8/10 . We said, "Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm."

It's a successful run of games that Konami is happy with, but getting here wasn't easy. After Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills failed to materialize, Okamoto said he had a hard time convincing higher-ups that more games was the way to go. However, as far as he was concerned, "just one remake is not enough," adding, "as a producer, I cannot let it end only with that."

"If there were only one release, wouldn’t people think that the development is going to be cancelled again, I thought," Okamoto added.

While Konami's plan to launch additional waves of Silent Hill games spells a promising future for fans who have missed the franchise, we have known that the series would continue in some form. Bloober Team, the horror-centric developer responsible for the Silent Hill 2 remake, confirmed it was working on a remake of the original Silent Hill last year.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation: I Played a New Slice from the Early Game With a Boss Fight | IGN Preview
articles.summary: While our earlier previews described a giant open-world game absolutely chock-full of activities, it was nice to see that the story-intense linear bits are still there, and just as dramatic as they were in the first two games. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will ultimately be the conclusion to this massive remake trilogy, and I can just tell that some of the content that was maybe a bit rushed in the original PlayStation game is going to be massive.
articles.body:
Previous previews have focused on the open world, but my slice was focused on the more linear, story-intensive sections.

Difficulty was a bit lacking in this demo, but then again it was the first chapter of the game...

We’re about six months out from Final Fantasy VII Revelation, and while that doesn’t seem like a huge wait, the anticipation to play the final chapter of the FF7 remake is palpable, especially since the first chapter dropped six(!) years ago now. We’ve also had the chance to go hands-on with Revelation before, and while the first couple previews were focused on flying around the open world in the Highwind, I got to play a much more linear slice at New York Comic Con.

My demo opened up early in Chapter 1, when the party arrives at the North Crater, and it starts a linear path to the center of the giant hole. In both of the previews we’ve done already, IGN’s Michael Higham and Logan Plant both described Final Fantasy VII Revelation as this massive and overwhelming experience, but this first chapter felt more like walking into a late-game dungeon to fight a massive boss.

Even my party members felt like late-game versions of themselves, fully decked out in Materia and equipment. But it’s important to keep in mind that this is just an early demo, so the balance could totally change before Revelation comes out in April.

But before I actually started wandering into the depths of the crater, I couldn’t help myself in digging through the menus a bit – after all, that’s half the fun of RPGs, right? Clicking into the Materia menu, there’s actually a new way you can level it up, rather than slowly absorbing AP as you kill stuff. There are now Materia fragments, each of which you can consume to add one AP ratio to your Materia.

The remake’s third part didn’t really explain how I was supposed to gather these fragments, but I did start with 200 of them, so I just shoved all of them into my Fire Materia, which got it about a third of a level. I’m not sure I’d just dump them willy-nilly like that in the full game, because I’m not sure how rare they’ll be, but in a short 30-minute demo, what do I have to lose?

The Item Transmuter has also returned from Rebirth, but crucially, gathering the materials for it should be much less of a pain. The auto-loot option that, for some reason, you had to beat the campaign to unlock in Rebirth is just enabled by default in Revelation. I was able to just run through the level and hoover up crafting materials without mashing the triangle button. That’s a huge improvement.

After I was done poking around in the menus, I started to dive deeper into the crater, and it was gorgeous. Regardless of what I’m playing, there’s just something about levels with ice and crystals that always blows my mind, and delving through this crystalline labyrinth never ceases to amaze me – and I wasn’t even playing on the ‘Graphics’ optimization mode. Both Remake and Rebirth looked incredible, though, so it’s not surprising that Revelation is carrying that forward.

But even though I was wandering starstruck through the crater, it wasn’t long before I ran into a group of monsters. The default party in the demo was Cloud, Cid, and Vincent, and of course I immediately swapped over to the new characters to see how they play. Cid immediately stood out. He has this rhythmic quality to his combat, where after one or two standard attacks, you wait for him to be wrapped in this weird blue mist, and then attack again to unleash a stronger attack. And those stronger attacks seem really strong, staggering a standard enemy almost immediately.

I’ve already written about how Game Director Naoki Hamaguchi is going to make the platinum trophy easier to unlock . And it seems like that approach has carried over to combat. I was able to just melt through standard enemies without much thought. There were even larger enemies that spawned in with little mini-cutscenes, and I was able to dispatch them with just a couple of ATB abilities. Again, this is the first chapter, so it’s a little early to really get a feeling for how difficult the game will be when it opens up.

That difficulty (or lack thereof) made testing the new FITS system tricky. I wasn’t able to move FITS jobs around, but Cloud was assigned the Summoner job, and at the cost of one segment of the ATB meter, I was able to summon Ifrit, Shiva, or Titan to enhance my attacks. It was cool seeing some of my attacks land with explosions of fire or ice, but the real draw to this job, in my eyes, is the Synergy attacks each summon has.

Synergy attacks work just like they do in Rebirth and Remake, where you have to use abilities to fill up a little bar. Use enough of them on specific characters and you unlock powerful abilities. The appeal to the summons’ synergy attacks, though, is that I only had to build up ATB on one character to use them, which should make it a lot easier to just churn through them. But most enemies died before I was able to use enough abilities to get to the Synergy ability.

As I get deeper into the crater, I start running into Sephiroth clones – a ton of them – until Cloud has one of his signature visions of Sephiroth. I won’t go into too much detail on the particular nature of Sephiroth’s taunts here in the crater, but if you’ve played Final Fantasy VII on the PS1, you probably have a pretty good idea of what he’s saying.

Eventually, creatures start fusing with the Sephiroth clones to create even more monstrous enemies, until I end up face-to-face with Gigas. And, unlike a lot of the smaller enemies before this, I was able to work up to one of Cloud’s synergy attacks with Ifrit, which ended up being a sort of fusion of the summon’s classic Hellfire attack with Cloud’s sword. However, before the animation finished, Gigas died. But, you know, we’re getting there.

After facing a couple of subsequent enemies, I finally got to a whole crowd of Sephiroth clones surrounding a purple glow of some sort. A cutscene played, and, again, I’ll spare you the details, but it ended with Jenova Deathmourner hatching from one of the clones. Finally, something that can actually put up a fight!

The boss fight plays out pretty similarly to other Jenova battles throughout the series, only this time the tentacles that spawn and make the boss invincible breathe fire. The fight is comprised of three phases, and so I was finally able to actually use multiple synergy abilities – Cid and Vincent, along with Cloud and Shiva. And they’re just as bombastic as they are in Rebirth.

Eventually, after three phases of dodging fire and chopping down tentacles, the boss died and the demo was over. I would have liked the combat to be a bit more difficult, but it is still very early in the game, and there is likely going to be a lot of balance tuning as Final Fantasy VII Revelation gets closer to launch.

Finally, while our earlier previews described a giant open-world game absolutely chock-full of activities, it was nice to see that the story-intense linear bits are still there, and just as dramatic as they were in the first two games. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will ultimately be the conclusion to this massive remake trilogy, and I can just tell that some of the content that was maybe a bit rushed in the original PlayStation game is going to be massive.

articles.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
articles.summary: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through.
articles.body:
A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through.

Reddit user aogustoo shared their story in a post late last month. What began as a "shot-in-the-dark email" they sent to Rockstar asking for a signed GTA 6 poster has turned into what seems to be a heartwarming moment for them and the community.

"A while ago I took a complete shot in the dark and emailed Rockstar," they said. "I shared how hyped I was for GTA VI and asked if there was any chance I could get a poster for my room.

"Honestly, I expected an automated reply or nothing at all. To my absolute surprise, an executive actually answered and shipped an official GTA VI poster straight from their New York office to my home in Brazil."

You can see images, which show not only the poster but the emails they supposedly sent to receive it, above. As Rockstar (and the rest of the world) count down the days to GTA 6's November 19 launch, fans will no doubt be on the lookout for official merchandise like this. As many have pointed out, it's unclear if Rockstar truly took the time to send the poster, but the community is still looking to the moment as something worth celebrating as the countdown continues.

"This is a massive W tho," Rockstar content creator @videotech said on X/Twitter . "This guy isn’t an influencer or someone famous, literally just a random Rockstar fan. Very kind of Rockstar and Take-Two to take the time and effort to do this."

Comment by u/aogustoo from discussion in GTA6unmoderated

"​I blurred out all personal addresses, names, and contact emails to respect their privacy," aogustoo added. "Please don't flood their inbox with requests, as I'm pretty sure this was just a rare act of kindness from someone on their team."

There's still so much about GTA 6 that we don’t know, but one thing is for sure: Rockstar will probably get even more emails after this. You can also read about what Nintendo had to say about the chances of seeing GTA 6 on Switch 2 , some recently revealed radio stations , and even a batch of new screenshots .

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Returns to Marvel with Darkhold Destiny
articles.summary: Magic the Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny.

Rather than being based in a fairly mundane version of New York, Darkhold Destiny is taking the likes of Doctor Strange and the Asgardians and telling a more magical story (forgive me). What really separates this new out-there set from the other two Marvel sets is that Wizards of the Coast was really able to write its own story with Marvel's characters and settings, which makes them feel less like a crossover and more like a part of Magic's multiverse.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny New Cards

With a new story written in-house, Wizards of the Coast was also able to give its artists more license to create their own takes on Marvel characters. For instance, with Scarlet Witch in the Marvel Super Heroes set, she looks like a pretty standard take on her comic book appearance. But in the art I was shown for Darkhold Destiny, she looks much more like an MTG character, while still retaining some of the signature parts of her outfit – the mask is still there.

I was also given broad strokes of what the story is about. Essentially, Dormammu and Hela use the Darkhold to invade the entire multiverse, and it's up to Doctor Strange, Thor, and other Marvel heroes to stop them. Of course, because of the characters and, well, props that the story revolves around, the set is focused heavily on spellcasting.

Thematically, the spellcasting is focused on what's essentially three different 'schools' of magic: Arcane, Divine, and Dark. Arcane magic will be themed around Doctor Strange and his allies, while Divine magic will be wielded by the Asgardians and other similar... entities. Dark magic is primarily going to be wielded by the villains of the set, but there are some heroes, like Ghost Rider that will apparently be wielding Dark magic.

You can expect a lot of focus on cool instants, sorceries and 'unique enchantments.' Wizards is even bringing back the Arcane subtype on instants and sorceries, which hasn't been used since Saviors of Kamigawa all the way back in 2005. I even asked if WotC is bringing back the obscure 'Splice Onto Arcane' ability that let you combine different arcane spells, but sadly, it is not.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny Art

Just like any other recent set, there will be a whole lineup of different Darkhold Destiny products. The standard fare is all here, Booster Packs, Collector Boosters and Bundles; but there will also be four commander decks.

Each of these commander decks will also have a collector's edition available, which will be completely decked out in foils. There will also be two scene boxes, each with six mechanically unique cards. Both the Bundle and the special Gift Bundle will also come with a mechanically unique promo card, and I just hope they don't skyrocket immediately on TCGPlayer, but I know that they probably will.

Wizards of the Coast will be giving the first glimpse of its original Marvel story in February with a comic produced alongside Image comics. Then, another comic will come out closer to when the set launches in April 2027.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream advance to WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream have advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time in 13 years.
articles.body:
Angel Reese "manifested" that she would make it to the WNBA Finals. On Friday night, she delivered on that promise.

Reese and the Atlanta Dream swept the New York Liberty with a Game 3 win to advance to the WNBA Finals. It's the first time the Dream have made it since 2013.

"The job is not done. We're definitely happy about where we are right now, but we're not satisfied. I think we just continue to push every single day, get back to work," Reese said postgame. "But yeah, we're going to enjoy this moment tonight. And we put a lot of work in for the season. We can't shy away from knowing that we did put a lot of work to get to this moment. I'm really proud of this group."

Reese finished with a team-high 22 points, nine rebounds, three assists a steal and two blocks. DeWanna Bonner, who stepped in for the injured Allisha Gray, scored a double-double with 13 points and 13 rebounds.

Rhyne Howard, Jordin Canada and Isobel Borlase all finished with double-digit scoring.

articles.title: Valkyries deal out Aces, complete sweep in Las Vegas to advance to WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries extended a remarkable run in the WNBA playoffs Friday, beating Las Vegas 87-77 in overtime for a 3-game sweep and berth in the Fin...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS - They were ready. Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob and team president Jess Smith sat in courtside seats. So did E-40, the Bay Area's biggest, swaggiest basketball fan.

They came to see the Valkyries try to secure a berth in the WNBA Finals, a mind-bending possibility for a second-year franchise. This team didn't even compete in the league two years ago, and now it stood one win from advancing to the Finals.

Golden State smothered the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces in overtime to earn an 87-77 victory in Game 3 of their best-of-five semifinal series.

That completed the sweep for the Valkyries, in front of a boisterous crowd at Michelob Ultra Arena - including a loud, large contingent of violet-clad Valkyries fans.

The Valkyries will open the WNBA Finals next Saturday (Oct. 17) at Chase Center against Atlanta. The Dream advanced earlier Friday by eliminating New York.

Kayla Thornton led Golden State with 18 points, and Gabby Williams asserted herself down the stretch after struggling early to score 16. Kiah Stokes and Tiffany Hayes each added 11.

Freshly minted MVP A'ja Wilson scored 21 for the Aces, who also got 18 points from Jackie Young and 17 from Chelsea Gray.

The game careened into overtime only after a dramatic finish in regulation. Williams missed a difficult, driving layup with five seconds left and the score tied at 71-71. That set the stage for the Aces to take the last shot - but Gray's potential game-winner at the buzzer rattled around the basket and bounced out.

The Valkyries had erased a six-point deficit late in the fourth quarter, surging into a 69-69 tie with less than two minutes left. After Wilson missed a short jumper, Veronica Burton scored on an acrobatic, driving layup with 1:12 left to push Golden State ahead by two.

Las Vegas tied the score at 71 when Young slithered free to score on a layup with 27 seconds left.

Long before this back-and-forth, the Aces threatened to run away. The Valkyries trailed 47-36 in the third quarter, on the verge of disappearing from sight. Then they hopped to life, ripping off 17 consecutive points - yes, 17 - to momentarily take a six-point lead.

As usual, Golden State's effort was supremely democratic. Thornton buried a 3-point shot. Hayes followed with her own 3, then zipped past Wilson to score on a driving layup. Kaitlyn Chen did the same, then fed Stokes for an unlikely 3-pointer.

All the while, the Aces relied heavily on their marquee trio of Wilson, Gray and Young. Did those three players get tired in the second half? It seemed like a fair question as the Valkyries stormed back - and then not so much when the Aces quickly responded, surging back ahead by five.

Las Vegas head coach Becky Hammon did not disguise her intentions from the outset of Friday night's game. She unabashedly leaned into her team's size advantage, starting 6-foot-7 Kalani Brown alongside the 6-4 Wilson.

Brown played less than two minutes, total, in three games against Indiana in the first round. She played less than three minutes in Game 1 against Golden State - and more than 23 minutes in Game 2, when Brown and Wilson helped spark Las Vegas' spirited, second-half comeback.

The Valkyries again struggled to counter this two-big lineup. On one play, Brown backed Thornton (six inches shorter at 6-1) into the low post, established position and scored on an easy layup. Thornton couldn't do much, aside from suddenly having a growth spurt.

Beyond their size edge, the Aces played with predictable urgency Friday night - knowing a loss ended their bid for a fourth WNBA championship in five years. No player embodied this more than Gray, the 34-year-old point guard and Hayward native who spent much of her youth in the East Bay (and attended St. Mary's High in Stockton).

Gray scored 15 points in the first half, pushing the Aces ahead 45-36 at the break. Williams, who entered the game averaging 24 points in the playoffs, scored only four in the half, unable to find much space to shoot (2-for-7 from the field, including missing all three attempts from beyond the arc).

articles.title: Why all White Sox’s Will Venable, Guardians’ Stephen Vogt can do is ‘laugh’ at back-and-forth ALDS
articles.summary: All three other clashes in the division series, with only the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians vying for the fourth and final spot in the championsh...
articles.body:
All three other clashes in the division series, with only the Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians vying for the fourth and final spot in the championship series. It looked like the White Sox were in control of the series, winning two games at Progressive Field to set themselves up for a potential sweep heading back home, but the Guardians fought back and gave their division rival a dose of their own medicine — setting up a Game 5 on Saturday night.

Homefield advantage has been a mirage thus far through the first four games of the series. The White Sox will be hoping for a continuation of that trend, while the Guardians will be hoping to put an end to that to advance to the ALCS to set up a matchup against the Tampa Bay Rays.

All that the managers for both teams could do is laugh about their predicament, with the Guardians and White Sox set to go at it one last time in 2026.

"There's been a couple of times that Vogter and I have just looked at each other and laughed because this is just how it goes with these two clubs," White Sox manager Will Venable said, via MLB. "And I think it's a special thing."

"If you look at just the story of the battle that we've had with these guys throughout this season coming down to that last weekend for the division and then here we are with a Game 5 for a chance to go to the CS, I think it's fitting two really good clubs that are both just very competitive, really talented, and the heart and soul of the club and identity of the club comes through, and I think it's been cool to watch that play out in competition throughout the year."

Indeed, the White Sox and Guardians' competition for the AL Central crown went down to the wire . None of that matters now. It all comes down to one game to decide which of these two teams will go on further in their quest to win a World Series title.

articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering's next Marvel crossover set has been revealed , as Wizards of the Coast announced that "Marvel: Darkhold Destiny" will launch on April 9, 2027.

Preorders are now available via local game stores, TCGplayer , Amazon , and other retailers. I'll leave links to where you can buy everything just below.

"The world's greatest sorcerers conspired to keep the Darkhold sealed," Wizards of the Coast (WOTC) said in its announcement, as part of New York Comic Con. "But the dark side of the Marvel Universe has been unleashed!"

It also teased the arrival of "devils, sorcerers, and vampire-hunting vampires" in the upcoming set, which will of course explore the supernatural side of Marvel.

An original story has been developed for the new set, with WOTC developing in collaboration with Marvel, which will also introduce a brand-new original character. The story will also be adapted into a special Marvel Comics release, written by Jackson Lanzing and Collin Kelly.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny New Cards

"This story was crafted by our Narrative team with Magic in mind, and we're thrilled to see it adapted by two of Marvel's most beloved writers," added WOTC.

"You'll be able to follow this dimension-hopping narrative across the set, all while uncovering the secrets of the Dark Dimension and joining forces with Marvel's pantheon of gods."

The comic is due to arrive in February 2027 in digital format, followed by a physical release in April.

Magik, a mutant sorceress who many fans will also recognize from Marvel Rivals ' roster, or more recently Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls , is the only hero confirmed for the set so far.

But WOTC has also said that the expansion will feature plenty more "hotly anticipated" Marvel heroes and villains making their MTG debuts.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny Art

Marvel: Darkhold Destiny will include the main card set, Commander decks, Scene Boxes, and special collector-focused card designs.

The Commander precon options this time around are Lords of Hel (red-black), Gods of Asgard (red-green-white), Strange Academy (white-blue-black) and Midnight Sons (white-black).

WOTC says it has also developed new "Booster Fun treatments" for the expansion, alongside updated versions of designs used in previous releases, "so collectors of everything Marvel will have plenty to get excited for".

Darkhold Destiny is one of the latest collaborations between Marvel and Magic: The Gathering, which has been increasingly drawing established entertainment franchises to the TCG through its Universes Beyond range.

In 2025, we saw the Marvel Spider-Man set , and in 2026, we got the Marvel Super Heroes expansion as well.

Now in 2027, Darkhold Destiny continues the longstanding collaboration between the entertainment giants.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

articles.title: The Telo MT1 is a big truck trapped in a tiny truck’s body
articles.summary: The Telo MT1 measures just 152 inches long — same as a Mini Cooper — and packs 500 horsepower. In our review, we test how the MT1 combines full-size utility with ultra-compact agility.
articles.body: I’m bouncing down the road in San Carlos, California, zipping past behemoth tech companies like EA and Oracle, in America’s smallest electric truck. The Telo MT1 (which stands for “mini truck”) unquestionably turns heads because it looks so remarkably different from everything else on the market right now. It has a nearly cab-over design, meaning that front-seat passengers sit almost directly over the front axle. It looks a lot like a Japanese kei truck, with a super-short nose and four doors. People stop to stare as we sit at stoplights or roll silently past. The interior is surprisingly spacious, and while the seats are firm, they’re not uncomfortable, at least for short jaunts on the bumpy roads around Telo’s HQ. Telo Trucks cofounder and CEO Jason Marks drove us to the company’s offices ahead of my short one-block test drive, and from the passenger seat, the ride was firm but stable, thanks to a low center of gravity provided by the battery pack beneath the floor. Behind the wheel, the MT1 feels like a lighter, more nimble pickup truck with a stiff, slightly bouncy ride without any payload in the bed, combined with all the low-end power, torque, and acceleration of an EV. Once we circle back around to the road in front of Telo’s offices, Marks has me come to a full stop and stomp on the accelerator to get a feel for just how much power the little truck puts down, remarking that this was the same road where Tesla used to do its customer test drives of the Roadster many years ago. Marks says that the production version of the Telo will accelerate 0–60mph in an estimated four seconds. The truck easily rockets from a standstill, just like any other electric vehicle on the market today, a feat for a small startup with just 30 employees. Despite its diminutive appearance, the tiny Telo truck can go toe-to-toe with the giant SUVs and Teslas that populate this area. The Telo is, as Marks likes to point out, actually the same size as a two-door Mini Cooper, but far more practical with a tow rating of 8,000lbs, a full-size bed (96 inches), and a bevy of neat hidden features that Telo hopes will offer a viable, if somewhat pricey, alternative to the giant pickup trucks that dominate the American market. “I hope that our truck shows how amazing and fun and useful — especially useful — a small pickup truck can be, because the current big trucks are literally killing us,” Forrest North, Telo’s cofounder and CTO, said during our interview at Telo’s headquarters. “I mean, they’re fun to be up super high and look out and feel like you’re dominating the world, but they’re killing an extra, roughly, 5,000 people per year, so do we want to just give them a pass for that?” [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: How Telo was born Marks and North both live and work in the San Francisco Bay Area with their families, and both own pickup trucks: Marks because he has a 150lb three-legged dog he shuttles back and forth to the office every day, and North because he has a passion for the outdoors. Large pickup trucks can be useful, but they’re far from suitable for city life. That disconnect, as well as the founders’ passion for urban transportation, is what brought the two, along with Yves Behar, together to start Telo in 2022. Marks previously worked on automotive safety and validation at National Instruments, while North is a former battery engineer at Tesla, founder of Mission Motors (one of the first electric motorcycle companies to break the land speed record for an electric motorcycle), and cofounder of Recargo, which developed EV charging app PlugShare. Behar is the founder of fuseproject, an industrial design and brand development firm. Marks and North met through a mutual friend in the startup space and discovered they’d gone to the same high school in Washington, where they both pole-vaulted. It was a “kindred spirit moment,” according to Marks. "“I hope that our truck shows how amazing and fun and useful — especially useful — a small pickup truck can be, because the current big trucks are literally killing us.”" - Telo cofounder Forrest North Originally, their idea wasn’t about trucks at all — it was about electric motorcycles. Their initial pitch to an unnamed Silicon Valley VC firm included a slide deck comparing three concepts: an electric motorcycle, a small car, and a tiny truck. Everyone they talked to kept gravitating toward the tiny pickup. Sensing the enthusiasm, North pushed Marks to consider pivoting to building a truck, even though the motorcycle they’d planned was nearly complete. They even went so far as to poll about 200 people on the street and found that nearly 90 percent would rather have the truck. The next week, they pivoted from motorcycle to truck. “It’s clear to me that the trucks have just kind of jumped the shark,” North said. “The only thing they can do now is be big.” Telo aims to change the conversation about what electric transportation in urban centers can look like. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Battery, range, and layout For a small truck, the Telo MT1 packs a lot of range. At launch, the truck will come with a 77kWh battery pack, or a larger 106kWh pack that the company estimates will deliver up to 350 miles of range. The MT1 has a unique battery layout: a split pack with both 800V and 400V architecture. The 400V setup makes the Telo chargeable on Tesla’s V3 Supercharger infrastructure, while the 800V will let customers take advantage of new, higher-powered stations coming to market in areas like San Francisco. Telo currently builds its battery packs in-house. Each cell is individually fused so that a single failure won’t trigger a cascade across the pack. According to Marks, in-house manufacturing allows them to maximize energy density and longevity — a feat that hinges on thermal management. The passive thermal management system operates while the vehicle is parked, maintaining cooler temperatures even in direct sunlight, while active liquid cooling engages only when the vehicle is running. Additionally, North noted that Telo’s latest cells deliver roughly 20 percent more energy than those they sourced just a year ago. I drove one of two prototypes that Telo has been using for road testing. From the outside, the Telo looks smaller than its 152 inches of length suggest. With the lower rear section of the passenger seats (called the midgate) laid flat, you get a full-size, 96-inch truck bed. To make up for the lack of a frunk, which most EVs have, Telo also developed a “monster” tunnel (named because, like in a kids’ story, it’s a “monster under the bed”), which passes door to door beneath the front of the truck bed. It’s accessible from either side and is large enough for a pair of roll-aboard carry-on suitcases to slide in endwise. Marks said that while they knew the front of the MT1 would be difficult to engineer, adding the monster tunnel created a tough engineering challenge because it sits exactly where the battery pack connects. The interior is still being finalized, but Marks said that it will get two 13-inch digital displays that will support both Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. The steering wheel also has small scroll wheels, but most features will be controlled through the screen interface. How the Telo stacks up against the big trucks Japanese kei vehicles became a White House talking point late last year when President Donald Trump invited the tiny trucks to be built in the US. But making that actually happen is far more complicated because kei vehicles don’t meet US crash safety regulations. Marks claimed that Telo has solved this problem with a completely new front end and an innovative front hinge pillar that took nearly four years to develop and hundreds of thousands of hours of simulated crashes to verify. In the Telo, the redesigned hinge pillar does the structural job of a conventional one while also carrying the strut mount, the cross-car beam, and the dash — consolidating several separate parts into one. This allowed the company to cut the front-end part count roughly in half, Marks said. “We pretty much threw all [the conventional crash architecture] away and had to start from scratch,” Marks said. The company’s team includes Tesla’s former head of crash safety, brought on to help tackle the new front end and completely reengineer it. “We have effectively six crash [paths], two bumper beams and two shock structures, a completely different architecture of a hinge pillar, a completely different architecture of a torque box to distribute the energy appropriately to the various parts of the car and save that occupant compartment as much as possible,” he said, comparing the crash innovations to those in a Smartcar. “Would any other automaker say we’re going to bet the world on being able to rethink crash?” AI tools have made the virtual crash-testing process much more affordable for startups, and Telo recently locked in its body in white, the sheet metal shell made up of the major structural pieces of the truck (think of it like a skeleton of a vehicle). It’s currently being built by US supplier Schwab Industries in Michigan. Marks said Telo uses AI to run virtual crash tests around the clock, averaging roughly one test per hour. The next phase of crash testing will include cutting the body in white apart for what Marks called a “quasi-static validation,” and full crash testing (slamming the vehicle and its various parts into a wall to validate the virtual testing the company has done) will start next year before Telo starts customer deliveries. “I think it’s one of the most exciting times to start a hardware company,” North said. “It’s always been like, hardware is hard. That’s always been the cliché, and I wouldn’t say hardware is easy, but I would say it’s gotten so much easier because of software and AI.” [Image: Pricing, delivery, and other features The Telo MT1 will come in single-motor (rear-wheel drive) and dual-motor (all-wheel drive) layouts and offer add-ons like a solar-capable tonneau cover or camping shell. Reservations are open now for a refundable $152, and the base vehicle starts at $41,520. Marks said the company isn’t really worried about larger competitors like Ford’s upcoming midsized electric truck or Slate’s bare-bones EV because he sees their market entry as proof that a viable market exists for small electric pickup trucks. North argued that Telo is also in a better position than either Slate or Ford right now because the company has fewer parts moving in and out of the country; it’s assembling its own battery packs and building the body in white stateside, making it largely exempt from the Trump administration’s tariffs. “The pack is the most expensive part of the vehicle build and the heart and soul of the vehicle,” Marks said, “so we had to keep it in-house.” Marks said he’s been surprised by the volume of reservations: just over 14,000, with 70 percent of reservation-holders configuring AWD versions with the longer-range battery pack. He also noted that around 20 percent are first-time car buyers. Telo is aiming for profitability at around 5,000 vehicles within roughly 24 months of deliveries. The company plans to get vehicles into customers’ hands sometime in 2027, depending on the validation timelines, but the MT1 still has to go through EPA and California air quality certification. Most reservations have come from places like LA, New York, the Bay Area, Seattle, Dallas, Washington, DC, Miami, and Denver, with almost everyone opting for the larger battery pack, regardless of drive configuration. Marks pointed to Tesla as the trailblazer of EVs’ first real wave, proving electric cars could be fast, fun, and sporty. However, he believes the industry ultimately missed the chance to fully exploit their potential. Telo is tackling the problem by rethinking vehicle architecture from the ground up, returning to a “one-box” design made possible by eliminating wasted space. Ultimately, Telo’s focus comes down to purpose, according to Marks: “What does electric enable for the experience of the user, and what value does that bring?” While history has shown that the market isn’t kind to EV startups, in a world where giant American trucks increasingly barely fit in an average parking spot, the Telo MT1 and its creators are aiming to offer a capable electric pickup built for today’s cramped cities in the hope that Americans can get behind smaller and more capable electric vehicles.
